manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped per-cable integer counter 'consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C]' initialized to 0 for all cable indices C. After each round R: for each cable index C whose Kelvin pair is counted in kelvin_unrouted (both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO absent from routed nets) OR whose both members appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' (per the failing_reasons_symmetric scope of Rule 55), increment consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] by 1; for all other cable indices C not meeting either condition, reset consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] to 0. When consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] reaches 6 for any cable index C (or reaches 6 again after a prior injection reset it to 3 — i.e., fires at 6, then at 3+3=6 from last reset, and so on): (1) derive the cable-C shunt exit corridor as the 5mm-wide × 8mm-tall bounding rectangle centered on the geometric midpoint between cable C's shunt inner-edge pad centroids (the INA238 Kelvin tap window on the shunt inner face); (2) inject this rectangle as a routing keepout for round R+1 ONLY — do NOT ripup any existing tracks, only restrict future FR routing in that region for that one round; (3) reset consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] to 3 immediately after injecting (so it retriggers 3 rounds later if cable C continues to fail, giving FR two recovery rounds before re-injection); (4) log 'persistent_cable_kelvin_corridor_keepout' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) stall count at trigger, (d) keepout geometry (centroid + dimensions), (e) kelvin_unrouted and DRC from round R, (f) whether this is a first-trigger (count reached 6 from 0) or re-trigger (count reached 6 from 3). This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 47/48, and the DRC-regression keepout rule; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate. Rationale: Rule 33 correctly injects Kelvin force stubs every round cable C fails, but force stubs alone do not displace stable competitor tracks that FR has already placed in the cable-C shunt exit corridor and will not reroute voluntarily. After 6 consecutive rounds of failure — during which Rule 33's guidance fires every round — the corridor is demonstrably occupied; a one-round keepout forces FR to find alternative routing for those competitors, clearing the Kelvin exit zone without a full regional ripup. The 3-round cooldown after re-injection gives FR time to converge on the freed corridor before re-evaluating whether a second injection is needed. This is spatially distinct from the DRC-regression keepout rule (which targets the highest aggregate DRC locus, not necessarily cable C's shunt exit) and from Rules 47/48 (which require sustained high-DRC counter thresholds before a broader ripup).
